categories.pins: The Tiny Tapeout pin wrapper: the only module the shuttle sees
categories.interface: The serial host port: what lets a computer reach the timing unit with no CPU on the chip

builds.tile: Tiny Tapeout tile: exactly the files info.yaml submits

cross_cutting.title: Clock
cross_cutting.text: One clock domain: every flip-flop runs on the tile clock `clk`, 50 MHz target (info.yaml clock_hz). The serial bit time is fixed in silicon at 434 clocks, so the baud rate is clk / 434: 115,200 at 50 MHz, 57,600 at 25 MHz.

cross_cutting.title: Reset
cross_cutting.text: `rst_n` at the pins is active low and becomes the synchronous active-high `rst`. Reset is the only way to bring the host port back after a command was cut off half way: the port has no timeout (checked by make tour).

cross_cutting.title: Asynchronous inputs
cross_cutting.text: The serial input goes through its own two-flop synchronizer in tp_uart_rx; the eight capture inputs go through the two-flop synchronizers in sync_capture. Not analyzed here: metastability rates (MTBF), pad delay and oscillator error.

cross_cutting.title: Not present
cross_cutting.text: No CPU, no program memory, no QSPI, no security block, no debug port. The Xpulse instruction port of the shared timing unit is tied to zero; the host reaches the same functions through the register port.

tt_um_normansrule_tiqora_serial.title: Tiny Tapeout pin wrapper
tt_um_normansrule_tiqora_serial.summary: Puts the serial port on the Tiny Tapeout UART pins and the timing unit's triggers, capture inputs and queue status on the rest.
tt_um_normansrule_tiqora_serial.example: On the demo board the RP2040 bridges ui_in[3] and uo_out[4] to USB-C, so a computer talks to the chip with no adapter.
stages: rst_n inverted to the synchronous active-high rst
capture inputs: ui_in[2:0], ui_in[7:4] and uio_in[0]; ui_in[3] is the serial input
uio_oe is fixed at 1111_1110: uio[0] in, the other seven out
tt_um_normansrule_tiqora_serial.reset: uio_oe does not depend on reset.

port_notes.ui_in: [8] CAP0, CAP1, CAP2, RX, CAP3, CAP4, CAP5, CAP6
port_notes.uo_out: [8] TRIG0, TRIG1, TRIG2, EVT, TX, OVF, HB, EVTP
port_notes.uio_out: [8] bit 1 ACT, bits 4:2 EVCH, bit 5 EVED, bits 7:6 EVQ; bit 0 is an input (CAP7)

tp_sync_soc.title: Serial system top
tp_sync_soc.summary: Connects the host port to the timing unit's register port and puts the head of the event queue on pins for a logic analyzer.
tp_sync_soc.example: When a capture lands, EVTP (uo_out[7]) pulses for one clock and EVQ (uio[7:6]) goes to 1, with no host polling.
stages: EVTP: one-clock pulse when the queue goes from empty to not empty
HB: timebase bit 23

EVCH/EVED/EVQ: fields of the queue head and count. EVCH and EVED are meaningful only while EVQ is not 0: the queue storage has no reset, so before the first event they are undefined, and after the last pop they still show the popped event
tp_sync_soc.handshake: Wiring plus one flip-flop for the EVTP edge.
tp_sync_soc.latency: EVTP pulses the clock after EVT rises.

tp_host_uart.title: Serial host port
tp_host_uart.summary: Turns bytes from the host into register reads and writes on the timing unit, with an ACK, a NAK or the data in reply.
tp_host_uart.example: 01 04 a0 bb 0d 00 writes 0x000dbba0 into CMP0 (arms TRIG0) and the chip answers 06; 02 01 pops the oldest event and returns it in four bytes, least significant first.
stages: H_CMD: wait for a command byte
H_ADDR: wait for the register offset
H_DATA: collect four data bytes (writes)
H_DO: one clock on the register port
H_SEND: send the reply bytes
tp_host_uart.handshake: Host to chip: 0x01 addr d0 d1 d2 d3 write, 0x02 addr read, 0x03 ping. Chip to host: 0x06 ACK, d0..d3, 0x5A 0x01 (magic, version), or 0x15 NAK. No flow control; one command at a time.
tp_host_uart.latency: Each byte is 10 bits of 434 clocks (86.8 us at 50 MHz). A write is 6 bytes in and 1 out; a read is 2 in and 4 out.
tp_host_uart.errors: An unknown command byte answers NAK 0x15. Only offsets 0, 1 and 2 can be read; every other offset reads 0. A write to an offset with no register behind it (0, 1, 2, 6, 11 to 15) is acknowledged and does nothing.
tp_host_uart.stall: There is no timeout. A command cut off part way leaves the port waiting for the missing bytes, and whatever the host sends next is taken as those bytes; bytes that arrive while a reply is being sent are dropped. Only reset clears it (checked by make tour).

port_notes.reg_addr: [4] register offset: 0 TIME, 1 EVENT (pops), 2 STAT, 3 CFG, 4 CMP0, 5 CMP1, 7 PW, 8 ADJ, 9 RATE, 10 PULSE
port_notes.active: [1] high while a command or reply is in progress (ACT pin)

tp_uart_rx.title: Serial receiver
tp_uart_rx.summary: 8N1 receiver with its own two-flop synchronizer and a fixed bit time of DIV clocks.
tp_uart_rx.example: At 50 MHz a bit is 434 clocks; each data bit is sampled in its centre.
stages: IDLE: wait for the line to go low
START: confirm it is still low half a bit later
DATA: eight bits, least significant first
STOP: valid pulses for one clock
tp_uart_rx.handshake: valid for one clock with data.
tp_uart_rx.latency: A byte is ready during its stop bit.
tp_uart_rx.errors: A start bit gone at its half-bit check is ignored as a glitch.

port_notes.data: [8] valid only in the valid clock

tp_uart_tx.title: Serial transmitter
tp_uart_tx.summary: 8N1 transmitter with the same fixed bit time as the receiver.
tp_uart_tx.example: Pulse start with 0x06 while busy is low: start bit, 0,1,1,0,0,0,0,0, stop bit.
stages: start bit
8 data bits, least significant first
stop bit
tp_uart_tx.errors: A start while busy is ignored.

sync_unit.title: Timing unit
sync_unit.summary: Joins the timebase, capture lanes, event queue and three deadline comparators behind one register port that the host reaches over serial.
sync_unit.example: A read of offset 0 returns the live 32-bit timebase at the clock the host port's H_DO happens.
stages: decode the register port
arbitrate simultaneous capture events: lowest channel first, one per clock, same timestamp
push events into one queue
sync_unit.handshake: Register port: single-clock reg_req. The Xpulse instruction port is tied to zero in this build.
sync_unit.latency: Same clock for every register access.
sync_unit.reset: Timebase 0, queue empty, triggers disarmed, capture disabled, pulse width 8.
sync_unit.errors: Queue overflow is sticky (OVF pin, status bit 6). Reading EVENT on an empty queue returns 0.

port_notes.status_out: [32] bits 1:0 count, 4 empty, 5 full, 6 overflow, 10:8 armed, 14:12 trigger levels, 23:16 synchronized pin levels

sync_timebase.title: Timebase with rate trim
sync_timebase.summary: A 32-bit tick counter that advances one tick per clock, can be stepped through ADJ and slewed through RATE in steps of 2^-24 tick per clock.
sync_timebase.example: RATE = 0x0080_0000 (2^23) makes the timebase run at 1.5 ticks per clock.
stages: free run: +1 per clock
rate: a 24-bit fractional accumulator; on overflow +2 (positive) or 0 (negative)
step: ADJ adds a signed value plus the clock's own tick
sync_timebase.handshake: rate_we and adj_we are one-clock strobes.
sync_timebase.errors: Wraps after 2^32 ticks (85.9 s at 50 MHz); the comparators are wrap-safe within 2^31 ticks.

sync_capture.title: Capture lanes
sync_capture.summary: Turns each asynchronous capture pin into a clean edge event through a two-flop synchronizer and an edge detector.
sync_capture.example: An edge on CAP0 is in the queue within a few clocks, and EVT and EVTP show it at the pins (checked by make tour).
stages: two-flop synchronizer
optional glitch filter (FILTW, 0 in this build)
edge detect: rising, falling or both, per channel
sync_capture.latency: Constant two clocks from pin to event with FILTW = 0.
sync_capture.reset: No events; channels disabled until CFG is written.
sync_capture.errors: A pulse shorter than one clock can be missed.

sync_event_fifo.title: Event queue
sync_event_fifo.summary: One shared queue of 32-bit timestamped events, two deep, that keeps the order of events across channels.
sync_event_fifo.example: The host reads offset 1 to pop the oldest event: bit 31 source, 30:28 channel, 27 edge, 26:0 timestamp.
stages: push when not full
pop when not empty
overflow when a push finds it full
sync_event_fifo.handshake: push and pop strobes; rdata is the head while not empty.
sync_event_fifo.latency: An event is readable the clock after it is pushed.
sync_event_fifo.errors: A push into a full queue drops the event and sets overflow, which stays set until reset.

port_notes.wdata: [32] bit 31 source, 30:28 channel, 27 rising edge, 26:0 timestamp

sync_compare.title: Deadline comparators
sync_compare.summary: Three trigger channels: arm one with an absolute tick and its pin goes high on exactly that tick for the programmed pulse width.
sync_compare.example: Write CMP0 = TIME + 60000: TRIG0 rises at the pin on the tick the timebase equals 60000 past the value read, 8 ticks wide (checked by make tour).
stages: arm: store the deadline, set armed
compare: reached = signed((now + 1) - deadline) >= 0
fire: load the pulse counter, disarm
count down the pulse width
sync_compare.handshake: arm_we with arm_time and arm_sel; pulse_we fires channels at once.
sync_compare.latency: The pin edge lands on the programmed tick.
sync_compare.errors: Wrap-safe within 2^31 ticks. The register map reaches CMP0 and CMP1 only (offset 6 is unmapped); TRIG2 fires only through PULSE.
